name: Fred's
why_fit: Fred's is a Marin County boutique that explicitly curates 'small-production clothing and exceptional goods from independent designers and makers,' which maps directly onto Ocean SF's made-to-order, small-batch model and woman-owned independent brand identity. Mill Valley sits at the edge of the bay, and its customer base skews toward the kind of outdoors-engaged, quality-conscious, coastal Californian who already lives in the Ocean SF mindset. The store's deliberate curation of unfamiliar independent brands means there is a real buyer pathway, not just a conceptual one.
recommended_angle: Wholesale stocking, because Fred's actively champions small-production independent makers and its Marin location puts it directly in front of the coastal, eco-minded consumer Ocean SF is built for.
email_subject: Introducing Ocean SF, a small-batch sailing apparel brand coming this holiday season
email_body:
Hi there,

I wanted to take a moment to introduce Ocean SF, a woman-owned sailing apparel brand based in San Francisco. We make organic cotton midlayers and wardrobe essentials as a sustainable alternative to synthetic polyester outdoor apparel, which sheds microplastics into the ocean with every wash. Everything we make is produced in small batches, to order, through carefully chosen sustainable production partners.

I came across Fred's while researching independent boutiques in Marin that champion small-production, independent makers, and the fit felt immediate. The way you curate the floor around quality, craft, and brands that have a real point of view is exactly the kind of context Ocean SF belongs in. Your customers already understand the value of buying less and buying better.

We have a holiday collection of new organic cotton midlayers and basics launching later this season, and I wanted to make sure you knew who we were before it arrived. No ask at all at this stage, just an introduction. Once the line ships, I will follow up with specifics and would love to share the pieces with you then.

Thank you for the thoughtful work you do on Throckmorton. It's the kind of retail that makes a neighborhood.

Warm regards,
Kyla, Ocean SF Team

name: 7x7 Bay Area (Attn: Shoshi Parks, Executive Editor)
why_fit: 7x7 Bay Area is a women-owned SF lifestyle publication that recently appointed Shoshi Parks as Executive Editor, who has publicly committed to regular coverage of environmental sustainability and local founders doing innovative work. The outlet has already published a piece on SF sustainable fashion and the microplastics crisis in the fashion industry, making Ocean SF's organic cotton, zero-microfiber mission a direct editorial fit. 7x7 reaches 250,000 monthly readers, squarely the coastal, eco-minded Bay Area audience Ocean SF is built for.
recommended_angle: Press pitch: founder profile or holiday gift guide feature, framed around Sydney Chaney-Thomas's story as a woman-founded SF brand solving the microplastics-from-apparel problem, timed to coincide with 7x7's sustainability-forward editorial direction under Shoshi Parks.
email_subject: A San Francisco sailing brand making apparel without microplastics, ahead of the holidays
email_body:
Hi Shoshi,

Congratulations on your new role as Executive Editor at 7x7. Your recent note about the editorial direction ahead, specifically the commitment to covering local founders responding to the world's challenges in interesting ways, caught our attention, and we wanted to introduce ourselves.

Ocean SF is a woman-owned sailing apparel brand founded by Sydney Chaney-Thomas, based here in San Francisco. The brand makes organic cotton midlayers and wardrobe essentials as a direct alternative to the polyester outdoor gear that sheds microfibers into the Bay with every wash. Every piece is made to order, in small batches, with sustainable production partners. The ethos is simple: wear something beautiful, leave nothing behind in the water.

We have a holiday launch coming later this season, including new organic cotton midlayers and wardrobe basics, and we wanted to put Ocean SF on your radar before it ships. If the story of a SF-founded, water-rooted brand building a case against polyester resonates with what you are working on, we would love to be in touch. We are happy to share founder background, imagery, or anything else that might be helpful as you plan coverage.

Thank you for your time, and for the thoughtful work you are doing at 7x7.

Warmly,
Kyla, Ocean SF Team

name: Audrey Ruhland / Thisldu
location: SF Bay Area (Sausalito, CA roots; currently cruising East Coast)
why_fit: Audrey built her sailing identity entirely on the San Francisco Bay, living aboard a Rafiki 35 in Sausalito and documenting Bay life on @thisldu_ before cruising south. Her account has a confirmed history of apparel partnerships, including a collaboration with nautical brand Nantucket Whaler, and her audience is composed of fellow sailors, liveaboards, and coastal lifestyle enthusiasts who are exactly the people Ocean SF is made for. Her background in marketing gives her an unusually thoughtful eye for brand storytelling, which aligns well with Ocean SF's intentional voice.
recommended_angle: Influencer collab, gifting and soft content introduction. Audrey has demonstrated she partners authentically with apparel brands whose aesthetic matches her sailing life, making her a natural first touch for Ocean SF's organic cotton midlayer launch.
email_subject: A San Francisco sailing brand with your winter on the water in mind
email_body:
Hi Audrey,

I came across your work through Waterborne Mag and have spent some time reading through Thisldu. The way you write about building a sailing life on the Bay, from learning on the water in Sausalito to casting off the bowlines in 2019, resonates with the story behind our own brand.

I'm Kyla, reaching out on behalf of Ocean SF, a woman-owned sailing apparel brand founded in San Francisco. We make organic cotton midlayers and wardrobe basics as a considered alternative to the polyester-heavy gear that dominates the outdoor and sailing space. Everything we make is produced in small batches with sustainable production partners, and our whole ethos is built around the idea that what you wear on the water should reflect the same values you bring to it.

We have a holiday launch coming up, a new collection of organic cotton midlayers and essentials, and your audience feels like a genuine fit for what we are putting out. Nothing formal yet, just wanted to introduce ourselves now so that when the line is live, we can follow up with something concrete in case it feels right for your content.

Thank you for the years of honest, beautiful storytelling about life on the water. We'll be in touch once the collection ships.

Warm regards,
Kyla, Ocean SF Team

name: ELI (shopeli.com)
why_fit: ELI is a woman-owned boutique in downtown Mill Valley whose owner, Eli Loftus, personally curates every piece with a deliberate focus on female-founded and independent brands, selecting for timeless wearability over trend. The store's coastal Marin clientele, relaxed sophistication, and emphasis on quality wardrobe staples align closely with Ocean SF's organic cotton midlayers and 'Wear Your Values' ethos. Mill Valley sits minutes from the water and draws the same eco-minded, active coastal consumer Ocean SF is built for.
recommended_angle: Wholesale stocking. ELI's existing curation of independent, female-founded brands with a California-cool, timeless sensibility makes it a natural shelf partner for Ocean SF's organic cotton midlayers, particularly heading into the holiday gifting season.
email_subject: A San Francisco sailing brand coming to you this holiday season
email_body:
Hi Eli,

I wanted to take a moment to introduce Ocean SF, a woman-owned apparel brand founded here in San Francisco. We make organic cotton midlayers and wardrobe essentials as a considered alternative to the synthetic polyester pieces that dominate outdoor and coastal apparel. Every garment is made to order, in small batches, with sustainable production partners, and is designed to live in a wardrobe for years rather than seasons.

I came across ELI while researching boutiques that approach curation the way we approach design: with intention, a strong point of view, and a genuine preference for independent, female-founded work. The brands you carry and the sensibility you've built on Throckmorton feel like a natural home for what we make.

We have a holiday collection of new organic cotton midlayers and basics launching soon, and I wanted to reach out before it goes live so this introduction lands with some context. Once the line ships, I'll follow up with the full details. No ask today, simply wanted you to know we exist and that we had you in mind.

Thank you for the thoughtful shop you've built in Mill Valley. I look forward to sharing more when the time is right.

Warmly,
Kyla, Ocean SF Team
